title: メディア情報論Ⅰ
subtitle: Media Informatics I
keywords: Media Information 2.Visual, Auditory, Tactile, and Multisensory Perception 3.Fourier Analysis and Information Theory 4.Information Processing in Computers
educationalGoal: The aim of this course is to explore information theory from a scientific perspective on human sensation and to develop an understanding of the fundamental principles underlying both human perceptual processing and computer-based information processing. Students will learn about human information processing—such as visual, auditory, tactile, and multisensory integration—as well as computational processing of images, video, and sound, fostering the ability to analyze and reflect on these mechanisms.
advice: This course introduces theories of computer-based information processing—such as text, images, video, and sound—beginning with an understanding of human sensory information processing. Students will study psychological and physical foundations related to vision, hearing, touch, and multisensory integration, and learn essential concepts for handling these modalities computationally, including binary representation, Fourier analysis, information theory, image processing, and speech processing. Through this, students will gain a theoretical perspective for understanding how media content is transmitted to and perceived by humans. Because this course is closely connected to Media Information II, which focuses on human perception, students are encouraged to review the material and continue exploring the topics even after completing the course.
requiredKnowledge: This course assumes a basic understanding of binary and hexadecimal numbers. Familiarity with high school–level mathematics—such as exponents, logarithms, trigonometric functions, complex numbers, and summation notation—will help the learning process proceed more smoothly. Any topics not previously studied will be supplemented during the lectures. Students are expected to bring a laptop computer on days with lectures and exercises.

achievementLevels.standard: - Students will demonstrate understanding of human sensory information processing and information theory. - Students will be able to independently solve problems and assignments related to human sensory processing and information theory presented in this course.
